Doubled backslashes inside an r-string, inside the builder's `code(r'''…''')` block, emit LITERAL double backslashes into the generated notebook and will render as garbage in mathtext. corrections.claim: 'Bin populations for edges np.arange(13.0,14.8,0.2): [1162, 732, 446, 294, 150, 88, 32, 23, 3] (the last, >=14.6, is dropped by running_stat's min_n=8)'
corrections.correct_fact: The populations and the min_n conclusion are both CORRECT (verified), but the edge array is worth stating explicitly because it is a floating-point trap: np.arange(13.0, 14.8, 0.2) returns TEN edges [13.0 … 14.8] (14.8 is included by accumulation error), i.e. NINE bins, not eight. `running_stat`'s loop `range(1, len(edges))` therefore does reach bin 9 (14.6-14.8, n=3), which min_n=8 then drops. A further 3 halos with logM >= 14.8 (max 14.983) fall outside np.digitize's range entirely. So the CURRENT figure already omits 6 halos above logM 14.6 — worth noting alongside the 'the 5 halos above 5e14 would be silently dropped' warning.

THE NEW PANEL (c) CHANGES WHAT PANEL (a) MEASURES AGAINST. Panel (a) is Y_500c on an M_200c x-axis (unavoidable, correctly diagnosed). The new stellar panel uses m_star_200c, i.e. a 200c aperture on a 200c x-axis. So the finished fig03 will mix apertures ACROSS panels: (a) 500c-Y, (b) 500c-f_gas, (c) 200c-M_star. If aperture consistency matters more than the plan's 'consistent with the new x-axis' logic, m_star_500c is the alternative (median ratio 0.9669, %diff [-6.8 -3.3 -1.5 -0.3 -1.3 -0.1 +0.3 +4.7]) — but its BIND/truth trend is much weaker and less diagnostic. Recommend keeping 200c per the spec and stating all three apertures in one short on-panel line, since the mass-conventions footer is being deleted.

THE OLD PANEL (c) PLOTTED A NORMALIZED PROFILE, THE NEW ONE PLOTS A RAW ONE. Line 952-953 defines `norm1(prof) = prof/np.interp(1.0, r_cen, prof)` and panel (c) shows y(r)/y(r500c) — a SHAPE comparison, which is why the Arnaud curve could be overlaid at all. Step 10's new panel plots raw y(r) with no normalization. That is a defensible change (it now shows amplitude bias, which is the validation statement) but it is a change of meaning the spec never flags, and it silently retires the `norm1` helper. Any surviving prose about 'profile shape' must be rewritten to 'profile amplitude and shape'.
